Continue Nxeon's game-catalog provisioning integrity sweep. Fresh agent, no prior context — read this fully, then the state files, before acting.

*** CRITICAL — READ THIS FIRST: you are a background sub-agent. You do NOT receive external, Monitor, or custom-event notifications, and if you end your turn "waiting" for one, you simply HALT and the whole sweep stalls. This has already happened 3 times (once waiting on a Monitor event, once on a custom UNTURNED_DIAG_READY event). NEVER park waiting for an event. For a slow game install: poll it YOURSELF inside a single bash command with a bounded loop — e.g. `for i in $(seq 1 40); do <check-ready> && break; sleep 30; done` (cap the total wait ~20-30 min) — then read the result and continue in the same flow. If an install is genuinely too slow to finish in a reasonable window, record its in-progress state + your assessment in PROGRESS.md, TEAR IT DOWN, and move to the next family. Keep working continuously until you've swept the remaining families or hit a genuine blocker, THEN report. Do not end your turn expecting to be woken. ***

WHAT NXEON IS: a VPS/game-server hosting platform, codebase at /opt/nxeon on this primary Proxmox host (OVH Singapore). You run ON the primary; test VMs provision onto node-2 (178.63.94.114) via the platform's worker + Proxmox API. The harness, live DB, worker, and Proxmox access are all here on the primary.

NOTE: the previous run stalled mid-`unturned`; I already tore down its leaked test VM (vmid 108) and cleaned its DB rows. node-2 is clean now. Re-attempt unturned fresh (or skip if PROGRESS.md shows a verdict).

THE TASK per family: (1) provision for real on node-2, (2) poll until it's actually up (see the anti-parking rule), (3) verify the real join port is reachable from OUTSIDE the box, (4) — most important — change a real setting via the platform's own config-apply path and confirm it took effect on the live server (only palworld/minecraft/rust/valheim have a real-apply impl; for the rest, confirm whether one exists and document the gap — do NOT build new apply implementations), (5) tear down completely with teardown.sh.

READ FIRST: /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep/PROGRESS.md (full log + status), RESULTS.md, and the harness scripts there (sweep-one.sh, teardown.sh, provision.ts, wait.sh, verify.sh, info.ts, udpcheck.sh, teardown-db.ts) — read each before use. Also docs/DOCUMENTATION.md for write-up style.

ALREADY DONE (confirm via PROGRESS.md, don't redo): round 1 = 10 families; pass 2 touched ark, bedrock, conan, factorio, projectzomboid, satisfactory, terraria, tf2, vrising. REAL_APPLY_FAMILIES=["palworld","minecraft","rust","valheim"]. Known owner-decision items (skip, don't re-litigate): CS2 unsellable, Conan server binary won't start, catalog-wide disk-size audit.

REMAINING to sweep (skip any PROGRESS.md marks done): unturned (re-attempt), sdtd, enshrouded, gmod, theforest, sonsoftheforest, dragonwilds, sunkenland, abioticfactor, corekeeper, icarus, arkasa, soulmask, dst, vintagestory, necesse, l4d2, nightingale, squad, spaceengineers, kf2, barotrauma, sandstorm, mordhau, theisle, stationeers, eco, empyrion, tf2 (re-attempt). Watch arkasa/sdtd/icarus for disk-too-small; bedrock/conan/vrising cousins for root-owned-mount-vs-uid-1000.

- Never fabricate — every claim needs real evidence (off-box connection, RCON/log read-back, git log).
- Fix real bugs with minimal tested commits (tsc clean, tests at baseline), deploy staging→prod per PROGRESS.md, document in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md.
- Tear down EVERY test VM before the next family, always via teardown.sh (it also purges vzdump backup archives — plain `qm destroy` leaves an orphan, which already leaked 8.4GB once). Never leave two test VMs running.
- Before finishing/pausing, verify node-2 clean: no leaked test VMs (`ssh root@178.63.94.114 'qm list'`), no orphaned Server/PortForward/Job rows, /tank/backup/dump/ holds only real-VM archives (leave sausaugepro vmid-101 — a real customer backup).
- Never touch a real customer server, never send a ticket reply, never rotate a live credential. Owner/pricing/business calls → document as "needs owner decision" and move on.

CONCURRENCY: a security-hardening effort runs in parallel, editing /opt/nxeon/lib and /opt/nxeon/scripts and writing docs/SECURITY.md. Stay in your lane (worker/game-config.ts, prisma/catalog.ts + seed files, docs/DOCUMENTATION.md); re-read a shared file right before editing it. Never run two prod builds at once — if a build/promote shows unexpected concurrent changes, pause and re-sync, don't force. If provisioning suddenly fails with Proxmox AUTH errors, the API token may have been rotated by the security work — STOP and report, don't retry in a loop.

REPORT when the remaining families are swept (or at a real blocker): what you did, bugs fixed w/ commit hashes, owner-decision items, families still unswept, and explicit confirmation node-2 is clean (no leaked VMs/rows/backups).

181	**Owner decision:** measured install requirements so far — **CS2 66.2 GiB / 58.42 GB prealloc,
182	ARK 22.9 GB, Project Zomboid >15 GB**. Setting advertised disk sizes the games actually fit in is a
183	pricing call.
184	
185	### Cross-cutting risk introduced mid-sweep by a CONCURRENT session (owner should know)
186	
187	At 08:10, while this sweep was running, another session committed `c59d9bc` ("Fix game orders being
188	provisioned to their linked basePlan's full size instead of what was actually sold"). It makes
189	`provision()` size game VMs from `gamePlan` (the advertised numbers) instead of `basePlan`. In
190	principle correct — customers should get what they bought. But measured against the live catalog:
191	
192	**116 of 121 game plans get a SMALLER disk under the new sizing**, often much smaller:
193	
194	```
195	  Abiotic Factor — 6 GB / 4 players     80GB -> 25GB
196	  ARK — 8 GB / 20 slots                 80GB -> 40GB
197	  Bedrock — 1 GB / 5 players            25GB ->  5GB
198	  Conan Exiles — 6 GB / 20 slots        80GB -> 30GB
199	  Dragonwilds — 6 GB / 5 players        80GB -> 25GB
200	  ...
201	```
202	
203	CS2's own gamePlan disks are 40GB/50GB — still far under its 58.42GB preallocation, so CS2 stays
204	impossible either way. But the general question is now live for every family: **is each advertised
205	disk actually big enough for that game's install?** Nobody has checked, and the games with the
206	largest installs (arkasa at 70GB advertised, ark, sdtd, conan, icarus) are exactly where it would
207	bite. From this point on this sweep provisions with the new sizes, so it tests what customers will
208	really get.
209	
210	Note: that commit reached production inside **this sweep's own promote** — the deploy scripts sync
211	to `main`, so a concurrent session's work rides along. Flagging rather than judging; it passed tsc
212	and the test suite alongside my own changes.
213	
214	### Bug #2 — eight families forwarded RCON, not the join port (FIXED, shipped `3be5383`/`c4d378c`)
215	
216	`GAME_PORT` is a health-CHECK map (prefers a TCP port because a TCP connect proves the game bound
217	it). Provisioning reused it as the forward-this-port map. For **rust, ark, projectzomboid, factorio,
218	arkasa, soulmask, squad, kf2** it names an RCON/query/admin port and the join port is a different
219	UDP one — `GAME_PORT`'s own comments always said so.
220	
221	Live proof on a fresh Rust provision: guest listening on BOTH 28015/udp and 28016/tcp; node-2 NAT
222	had exactly two rules (SSH + 28016/tcp); dashboard showed the customer `178.63.94.114:20019` — their
223	**RCON port** — as the address to give players. Same outage as real customer `rust-w75hko`, from
224	scratch.
225	
226	Fix: `joinPortFor()` + `GAME_JOIN_PORT_OVERRIDE` (8 rows, every one sourced from the family's own
227	`docker run -p` mapping), provisioning forwards the join port, `gameForwardFor()` selects it.
228	Verified: raw UDP from another host moved node-2's DNAT counter 0→6 packets AND tcpdump inside the
229	guest saw them reach the container (`eth0 In > 10.20.1.105.28015`, `docker0 Out > 172.17.0.2.28015`).
230	+3 tests.
231	
232	### Bug #3 — SECURITY: game RCON published to the internet with the image default password (FIXED, shipped `196e5c9`/`1e71d69`)
233	
234	Asking what was actually on the forwarded 28016: **Rust's WebSocket RCON answered from off-box and
235	returned a full `serverinfo` dump**, password `docker` (didstopia bakes `+rcon.password docker`;
236	`prisma/catalog.ts` never overrides). Ban/kick/any-convar/wipe control, from the internet, on the
237	port the dashboard was telling customers to hand to players. ark + projectzomboid seed
238	`changeme12` similarly.
239	
240	**Blast radius zero, narrowly** — the only real customer in these families (`rust-w75hko`) predates
241	auto-forwarding and holds only its join port (checked from the DB, no customer server touched). The
242	next order of any of the eight would have been exposed.
243	
244	Fix: retract the check-only forward after the check passes. End state = SSH + join port only.
245	Nothing internal regresses (`lib/game-control.ts` tunnels RCON to 127.0.0.1 over SSH). Verified:
246	rule gone on resync, the RCON that had just answered now unreachable, SSH + join port untouched.
247	
248	**Owner decision still open:** the images ship default admin credentials that survive regardless of
249	forwarding. Per-server generated RCON passwords surfaced in the panel = a feature, needs a product call.
250	
251	### Bug #4 — applyRust wrote a config file this image completely ignores (FIXED, pending verify)
252	
253	Two independent problems, both proven live:
254	1. **No `server.cfg` exists.** Rust ships none; the image creates only `bans.cfg`, `users.cfg`,
255	   `serverauto.cfg`, `relay_cfg.json` in `/opt/rust/server/docker/cfg/`. `remoteLocate` only matches
256	   existing files → every apply soft-failed "Could not locate Rust server.cfg".
257	2. **Fixing the path would not have helped.** Wrote `server.hostname "NXEON SWEEP TEST HOSTNAME"` +
258	   `server.maxplayers 42` into the real cfg dir, restarted, and RCON still reported
259	   `Hostname: Rust Server [DOCKER]`, `MaxPlayers: 500`. `didstopia/rust-server` builds its whole
260	   launch line from `RUST_SERVER_*` env vars (`/app/start.sh`, read directly off the container), and
261	   those win. Same class as Palworld's regenerate-then-lose bug.
262	
263	Fix: rewrote `applyRust` to the container-recreation pattern, and extracted
264	`recreateGameContainer()` + `readContainerEnv()` + `writeEnvFile()` as shared helpers so palworld
265	and rust cannot drift. Env mapping read out of the image's own `start.sh`:
266	`hostname→RUST_SERVER_NAME`, `maxplayers→RUST_SERVER_MAXPLAYERS`, `worldsize→RUST_SERVER_WORLDSIZE`,
267	`seed→RUST_SERVER_SEED`, and `pve` via `RUST_SERVER_STARTUP_ARGUMENTS` (the image's own escape hatch).
268	
269	Verified so far: container recreated `restart=no`, unit active `NRestarts 0`, ports preserved, no
270	stray container, env updated, and the **real running process's argv** now carries
271	`+server.hostname NXEON SWEEP RUST +server.maxplayers 42 +server.pve true +server.worldsize 4000`.
272	
273	### Bug #1 — game-config apply fought systemd for the container (FIXED, shipped)
274	
275	`worker/index.ts`'s `wrapDockerGameService()` turns EVERY family's `docker run -d --name X` setup
276	script into `docker create` + a `<hint>.service` systemd unit (`Restart=always`, `RestartSec=5`) and
277	deliberately strips docker's own `--restart` policy. So systemd — not docker — owns every game
278	container. `applyPalworld` talked to docker directly.
279	
280	- **The revival race the 2026-09-05 fix claimed to close was half-open.** Disabling docker's policy
281	  closes docker's half only. `docker stop` makes the unit's ExecStart (`docker start -a`) exit →
282	  systemd restarts it 5s later. Live journal during an apply:
283	  `05:23:19 Deactivated successfully` → `05:23:24 Scheduled restart job, restart counter is at 1`.
284	  The function had a 5-second budget to finish its rename+recreate.
285	- **Every successful apply re-added `--restart unless-stopped`**, permanently double-supervising the
286	  container — the exact state the provisioning wrapper exists to prevent. Confirmed on the real
287	  container post-apply: `restart=unless-stopped` + still-enabled `palworld.service`.
288	
289	Fix: shared `resolveGameUnit()` (resolves the unit from `controlSpec().serviceHints`), then
290	`systemctl stop` → `docker create` (no `--restart`) → `systemctl start`, plus a real
291	`.State.Running` confirmation before the rollback target is deleted. No unit resolved → old path
292	verbatim. Verified live: 4 settings read back off disk, `restart=no`, `NRestarts: 0`, clean
293	`Stopping → Stopped → Started` journal.

## Unturned was 100% dead — two independent root causes (2026-09-07)

Sweep pass 3. Every Unturned order failed the game-port check, and the container
crash-looped. Two unrelated bugs, both fixed.

**Bug 1 — the bind mount shadowed the game that ships baked into the image.**
Unlike the SteamCMD families, `imperialplugins/unturned` does **not** download the
game at runtime — it bakes the whole game into `/home/steam/Unturned` (the
`Unturned_Headless.x86_64` binary plus all `Bundles/Content/` are in the 4.85 GB
image; `init.sh` only `cd`s there and runs it). The setup script bind-mounted an
empty host dir over that exact path (`-v /opt/unturned:/home/steam/Unturned`),
which **shadowed the baked-in binary**, so the container looped forever on

```
./init.sh: line 21: ./Unturned_Headless.x86_64: No such file or directory   (exit 127)
```

Adding a `chown` would not have helped — the game files simply are not in the
mount. The mutable server data (worlds, config, players) lives in that dir's
`Servers/` subfolder, so the fix is to bind-mount **only** `/home/steam/Unturned/Servers`
and pre-`chown` it to uid 1000 (the image runs as `steam`). Verified live: the
container then runs `exit=0 restarts=0`, loads all 5577 assets, and writes its
instance dir into `/opt/unturned` as uid 1000.

**Bug 2 — the health-check/join port was TCP, but Unturned binds no TCP port.**
`GAME_PORT[unturned]` was `27015/tcp` "because a TCP connect proves the game bound
it." Unturned binds **UDP only** — confirmed by reading the container's own
`/proc/net/{tcp,udp}`: the sole TCP listener is `127.0.0.1:32971` (internal),
while `27015/udp` (game) and `27016/udp` (query) are bound on `0.0.0.0`. The
`-p 27015:27015/tcp` publish is a *dead mapping*: `docker-proxy` holds the host
TCP port, but a DNAT'd connection reaches the container and gets an RST. Proof by
path isolation on a live guest — in-guest `127.0.0.1:27015` connected (docker-proxy
accepts) but the guest's own `10.20.1.105:27015` and the external forward both
returned `ECONNREFUSED`, with node-2's DNAT rule correct and receiving packets.
So the TCP check could never pass and every provision failed after ~306s. Fix:
`GAME_PORT[unturned]` → `27015/udp` — the check now probes the port the game
actually binds, and since the join port then equals the health-check port, no
`GAME_JOIN_PORT_OVERRIDE` entry is needed (the forward is `27015/udp`, which is
what a player joins on).

**Fix locations (same two-place pattern as Terraria/Conan/TF2):** the setup
script in `prisma/seed-wave7-games.ts` **and** the live `OsTemplate` row; the port
in `lib/games.ts`. **Verified end to end** after deploy: a fresh provision through
the fixed pipeline reached `job=DONE`, the guest bound `27015/udp`+`27016/udp`,
`/opt/unturned` was owned by uid 1000 with the persisted instance dir, and the
UDP join port was reachable from off-box (node DNAT counter moved and in-guest
tcpdump saw the probes reach the container). No real-apply exists for unturned
(the `applyRealConfig` default case), so config-apply remains a documented gap for
this family, same as the other non-`REAL_APPLY_FAMILIES`.
